svg.content: <mxfile host="app.diagrams.net" scale="1" border="0"> <diagram name="Load Balancer Architecture" id="ZpmXwLPm35fRAqaLnkk5"> <mxGraphModel dx="1531" dy="867" grid="1" gridSize="10" guides="1" tooltips="1" connect="1" arrows="1" fold="1" page="1" pageScale="1" pageWidth="850" pageHeight="1100" math="0" shadow="0"> <root> <mxCell id="0" /> <mxCell id="1" parent="0" /> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-1" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=24;fontColor=#222222;fontStyle=1;spacing=4;" value="Load Balancer — Architecture in Simple Steps" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="36" width="1700" x="40" y="8" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-2" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=13;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Goal:</b> send every request to a server that can handle it right now &nbsp;|&nbsp; <b>Rule:</b> aim for the USER's speed, not for "equal turns" &nbsp;|&nbsp; <b>Remember:</b> every box below exists because the box before it was not enough" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="44" width="1880" x="40" y="48" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-3" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#b26a00;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#b26a00;" value="START HERE — why do we need a load balancer?" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="140" width="1910" x="20" y="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-4" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Problem:</b> with no balancer, every client picks a server on its own. All of them may pick Server A — A is overloaded while B sits idle." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="85" width="590" x="40" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-5" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision:</b> let ONE place decide where each request goes — the load balancer — because it can see which servers are free." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="85" width="590" x="680" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-6" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision:</b> aim for the USER's speed, not "equal turns". Equal turns can still send a request to a server that is busy." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="85" width="590" x="1320" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-7" edge="1" parent="1" source="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-4" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;endArrow=block;endFill=1;strokeWidth=2;strokeColor=#1a56a0;fontSize=11;fontColor=#1a56a0;labelBackgroundColor=#ffffff;" target="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-5" value="so"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-8" edge="1" parent="1" source="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-5" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;endArrow=block;endFill=1;strokeWidth=2;strokeColor=#1a56a0;fontSize=11;fontColor=#1a56a0;labelBackgroundColor=#ffffff;" target="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-6" value="and"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-9" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#1a56a0;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#1a56a0;" value="THE JOURNEY OF ONE REQUEST — read left to right, ① to ⑦" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="470" width="1910" x="20" y="260" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-10" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=11;fontColor=#222222;spacing=4;" value="<b>Blue</b> = what happens &nbsp;·&nbsp; <b>Green</b> = why we need it &nbsp;·&nbsp; <b>Yellow</b> = what it costs (the trade-off)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="24" width="1800" x="40" y="290" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-11" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>① Pick the city</b><br>DNS sends the user to the nearest healthy city (Chennai, else Mumbai)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="40" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-12" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="Distance adds delay on EVERY request — Chennai → Mumbai costs ~20 ms extra, however idle Mumbai is." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="40" y="460" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-13" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="DNS changes slowly, and the backup city is capacity we pay for but rarely use." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="40" y="595" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-14" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>② Pick a load balancer</b><br>DNS hands out several balancer addresses; each user gets one." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="310" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-15" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="On IPO day one balancer runs out of CPU and network long before the servers do." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="310" y="460" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-16" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="DNS spreads users roughly, not exactly — so each balancer still makes its own precise choice." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="310" y="595" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-17" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>③ The balancer pair</b><br>One ACTIVE balancer owns the address. A STANDBY watches it and takes over if it stops." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="580" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-18" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="The balancer can die too — then every healthy server behind it is unreachable." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="580" y="460" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-19" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="A few seconds of delay during takeover, plus a standby that sits idle. Only one may be active at a time." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="580" y="595" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-20" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>④ Overload check</b><br>If ALL servers are overloaded, reject some requests fast: "try again shortly"." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="850" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-21" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="Sending traffic to the "least busy" of busy servers just makes EVERYONE slow." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="850" y="460" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-22" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="Some users get a quick "no" — better than everyone getting a slow timeout." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="850" y="595" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-23" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>⑤ Find the right group</b><br>Read the web path (/ipo, /insurance…) and pick that group of servers." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="1120" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-24" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="Different servers do different jobs; the wrong group cannot answer." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="1120" y="460" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-25" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="Reading every request costs CPU. Do it only where needed; elsewhere forward blindly (faster)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="1120" y="595" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-26" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>⑥ Pick one server</b><br>Skip dead or draining servers. Choose by live load and speed. Session pinned? Use that server." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="1390" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-27" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value=""Next in line" counts requests, not work: a 5 ms check and a 2 s redemption look the same. A dead server looks idle." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="1390" y="460" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-28" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="Needs live numbers and health checks. Pinning a session fights load-awareness." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="1390" y="595" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-29" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>⑦ Send and learn</b><br>Forward the request; record how long it took and whether it failed." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="1660" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-30" parent="1" value="These numbers feed step ⑥ and the health checks — the balancer keeps learning." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="240" x="1660" y="460" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#2e7d32;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#2e7d32;" value="BEHIND THE SCENES — what keeps the steps honest" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="330" width="1910" x="20" y="750" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-39" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Health checks</b> — feed steps ③ and ⑥<br>Two ways to know a server is alive: ask it every few seconds (ACTIVE) and watch real requests fail (PASSIVE)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="105" width="590" x="40" y="795" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-40" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="Active finds a dead server at 3 a.m. when there is no traffic; passive reacts within seconds when traffic is heavy." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="75" width="590" x="40" y="910" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-41" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="Active costs steady probe traffic (200 servers every 2 s = 100 pings/s). Passive is blind when traffic is low. So we use both." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="75" width="590" x="40" y="995" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-42" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Safe deploy (draining)</b> — feeds step ⑥<br>Mark the server DRAINING → no NEW requests → current ones finish → then update. After a time limit, force-close the stragglers." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="105" width="590" x="680" y="795" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-43" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="Killing a server mid-redemption breaks a real request: the user and the ledger now disagree." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="75" width="590" x="680" y="910" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-44" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="Deploys take longer, and a few slow requests are cut on purpose — but only after a known time limit." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="75" width="590" x="680" y="995" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-45" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Remembering the user</b> — feeds step ⑥<br>Best: keep sessions in a shared store so ANY server can serve ANY request. Fallback: "sticky" — always the same server." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="105" width="590" x="1320" y="795" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-46" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="A multi-step flow (like KYC) breaks if the next request lands on a server that has never seen the user." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="75" width="590" x="1320" y="910" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-47" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="Sticky ties users to one server and can pile load on it. A shared store is one more system to run." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="75" width="590" x="1320" y="995" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-48" parent="1" value="deploy" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="34" width="180" x="1712" y="1376" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-70" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=16;fontColor=#222222;fontStyle=1;spacing=4;" value="How to read it" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="900" x="40" y="1485" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-71" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Follow the steps ①–⑦</b><br>① The user asks for one address; DNS answers with the nearest healthy city.<br>② Inside the city, DNS hands out several balancer addresses so no single balancer is overloaded.<br>③ Each address is a pair: one ACTIVE balancer and one STANDBY ready to take over.<br>④ Overloaded? Reject some requests quickly instead of making everyone wait.<br>⑤ Read the web path and pick the right group of servers.<br>⑥ Pick a healthy server with the least real work — not just the next in line.<br>⑦ Send the request and note how it went; this helps the next decision.<br><b>Example:</b> IPO allotment day, 40× traffic → nearest city → one of several balancers → /ipo goes to the IPO group → if every server passes 100%, extra requests get a fast "try again"." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="240" width="935" x="40" y="1525" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-72" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Why this order? Build it in this order</b><br>1. Clients guess → one place decides (the balancer).<br>2. Equal turns ignore real work → choose by live load (⑥).<br>3. A dead server looks idle → add health checks.<br>4. Different jobs need different servers → read the path (⑤).<br>5. The balancer itself can die → active + standby (③).<br>6. One balancer is too small → several, spread by DNS (②).<br>7. All servers drowning → reject fast (④).<br>8. Servers in two cities → pick the city first (①).<br><i>Every box exists because the one before it was not enough.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="240" width="935" x="995" y="1525" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-73" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Architect decisions — say "why A over B"</b><br>1. User speed over equal turns. 2. Live load over round-robin (count ≠ work).<br>3. Connection count is only a proxy — 11 slow calls can be heavier than 42 idle ones.<br>4. Health is a separate signal from load; use active AND passive checks.<br>5. L4 (fast, blind) by default; L7 (reads the path) only where it pays off.<br>6. Shared session store over sticky sessions.<br>7. Standby pair for availability; several pairs for scale.<br>8. Drain servers, never kill them. 9. Reject fast over slow-for-everyone.<br>10. Choose the city first, then the server — different problems, different speeds." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="240" width="935" x="40" y="1785" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="yEF4O2vbRbdOwqUzVLqb-74" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Trade-offs we accept</b><br>• Live-load routing → more numbers to track · L7 → CPU cost · health checks → probe traffic + blind spots<br>• Standby + backup city → idle capacity and a few seconds of takeover<br>• DNS spread → rough balance · Rejecting → some users get "try again" · Draining → slower deploys<br><br><b>One-line close:</b> "A load balancer keeps 'where should this go?' close to 'who can take it right now?' — and each part exists because the one before it was not enough."<br><br><b>Honest test:</b> every server is at 130% — does it send everyone to the "least bad" one? It must not: it rejects fast and protects the servers.<br><b>Extend later:</b> TLS termination · per-client rate limits · consistent hashing · canary routing." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="240" width="935" x="995" y="1785" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div: START HERE — why do we need a load balancer?

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(248, 206, 204), rgb(81, 45, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

div.div: Problem: with no balancer, every client picks a server on its own. All of them may pick Server A — A is overloaded while B sits idle.

div.div: Decision: let ONE place decide where each request goes — the load balancer — because it can see which servers are free.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 175px; margin-left: 1310px;

div.div: Decision: aim for the USER's speed, not "equal turns". Equal turns can still send a request to a server that is busy.

div.div:
① Pick the city
DNS sends the user to the nearest healthy city (Chennai, else Mumbai).

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 512px; margin-left: 30px;

div.div: Distance adds delay on EVERY request — Chennai → Mumbai costs ~20 ms extra, however idle Mumbai is.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 647px; margin-left: 30px;

div.div: DNS changes slowly, and the backup city is capacity we pay for but rarely use.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 377px; margin-left: 299px;

div.div:
② Pick a load balancer
DNS hands out several balancer addresses; each user gets one.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 512px; margin-left: 300px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: On IPO day one balancer runs out of CPU and network long before the servers do.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 647px; margin-left: 300px;

div.div:
③ The balancer pair
One ACTIVE balancer owns the address. A STANDBY watches it and takes over if it stops.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 512px; margin-left: 570px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The balancer can die too — then every healthy server behind it is unreachable.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 647px; margin-left: 570px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: A few seconds of delay during takeover, plus a standby that sits idle. Only one may be active at a time.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 377px; margin-left: 839px;

div.div:
④ Overload check
If ALL servers are overloaded, reject some requests fast: "try again shortly".

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 512px; margin-left: 840px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Sending traffic to the "least busy" of busy servers just makes EVERYONE slow.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 647px; margin-left: 840px;

div.div: Some users get a quick "no" — better than everyone getting a slow timeout.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 377px; margin-left: 1109px;

div.div:
⑤ Find the right group
Read the web path (/ipo, /insurance…) and pick that group of servers.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.div: Different servers do different jobs; the wrong group cannot answer.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 647px; margin-left: 1110px;

div.div: Reading every request costs CPU. Do it only where needed; elsewhere forward blindly (faster).

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 377px; margin-left: 1379px;

div.div:
⑥ Pick one server
Skip dead or draining servers. Choose by live load and speed. Session pinned? Use that server.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 512px; margin-left: 1380px;

div.div: "Next in line" counts requests, not work: a 5 ms check and a 2 s redemption look the same. A dead server looks idle.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 647px; margin-left: 1380px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Needs live numbers and health checks. Pinning a session fights load-awareness.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 377px; margin-left: 1649px;

div.div:
⑦ Send and learn
Forward the request; record how long it took and whether it failed.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 512px; margin-left: 1650px;

div.div: These numbers feed step ⑥ and the health checks — the balancer keeps learning.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 222px; height: 1px; padding-top: 647px; margin-left: 1650px;

div.div: A little bookkeeping on every request.

div.div: BEHIND THE SCENES — what keeps the steps honest

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 840px; margin-left: 30px;

div.div:
Health checks — feed steps ③ and ⑥
Two ways to know a server is alive: ask it every few seconds (ACTIVE) and watch real requests fail (PASSIVE).

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 940px; margin-left: 30px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Active finds a dead server at 3 a.m. when there is no traffic; passive reacts within seconds when traffic is heavy.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1025px; margin-left: 30px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Active costs steady probe traffic (200 servers every 2 s = 100 pings/s). Passive is blind when traffic is low. So we use both.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 840px; margin-left: 670px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Safe deploy (draining) — feeds step ⑥
Mark the server DRAINING → no NEW requests → current ones finish → then update. After a time limit, force-close the stragglers.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 940px; margin-left: 670px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Killing a server mid-redemption breaks a real request: the user and the ledger now disagree.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1025px; margin-left: 670px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Deploys take longer, and a few slow requests are cut on purpose — but only after a known time limit.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 840px; margin-left: 1310px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Remembering the user — feeds step ⑥
Best: keep sessions in a shared store so ANY server can serve ANY request. Fallback: "sticky" — always the same server.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 940px; margin-left: 1310px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: A multi-step flow (like KYC) breaks if the next request lands on a server that has never seen the user.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1025px; margin-left: 1310px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Sticky ties users to one server and can pile load on it. A shared store is one more system to run.

div.div: How to read it

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 917px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1637px; margin-left: 30px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Follow the steps ①–⑦
① The user asks for one address; DNS answers with the nearest healthy city.
② Inside the city, DNS hands out several balancer addresses so no single balancer is overloaded.
③ Each address is a pair: one ACTIVE balancer and one STANDBY ready to take over.
④ Overloaded? Reject some requests quickly instead of making everyone wait.
⑤ Read the web path and pick the right group of servers.
⑥ Pick a healthy server with the least real work — not just the next in line.
⑦ Send the request and note how it went; this helps the next decision.
Example: IPO allotment day, 40× traffic → nearest city → one of several balancers → /ipo goes to the IPO group → if every server passes 100%, extra requests get a fast "try again".

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 917px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1637px; margin-left: 985px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Why this order? Build it in this order
1. Clients guess → one place decides (the balancer).
2. Equal turns ignore real work → choose by live load (⑥).
3. A dead server looks idle → add health checks.
4. Different jobs need different servers → read the path (⑤).
5. The balancer itself can die → active + standby (③).
6. One balancer is too small → several, spread by DNS (②).
7. All servers drowning → reject fast (④).
8. Servers in two cities → pick the city first (①).
Every box exists because the one before it was not enough.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 917px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1897px; margin-left: 30px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Architect decisions — say "why A over B"
1. User speed over equal turns. 2. Live load over round-robin (count ≠ work).
3. Connection count is only a proxy — 11 slow calls can be heavier than 42 idle ones.
4. Health is a separate signal from load; use active AND passive checks.
5. L4 (fast, blind) by default; L7 (reads the path) only where it pays off.
6. Shared session store over sticky sessions.
7. Standby pair for availability; several pairs for scale.
8. Drain servers, never kill them. 9. Reject fast over slow-for-everyone.
10. Choose the city first, then the server — different problems, different speeds.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 917px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1897px; margin-left: 985px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Trade-offs we accept
• Live-load routing → more numbers to track · L7 → CPU cost · health checks → probe traffic + blind spots
• Standby + backup city → idle capacity and a few seconds of takeover
• DNS spread → rough balance · Rejecting → some users get "try again" · Draining → slower deploys
One-line close: "A load balancer keeps 'where should this go?' close to 'who can take it right now?' — and each part exists because the one before it was not enough."
Honest test: every server is at 130% — does it send everyone to the "least bad" one? It must not: it rejects fast and protects the servers.
Extend later: TLS termination · per-client rate limits · consistent hashing · canary routing.
